metadata.description: First Deputy Chief Justice of South Africa (1997-2000) and Acting Chief Justice.
Chief Justice of South Africa (2005-2009), human rights lawyer, and member of the first Constitutional Court bench.
Deputy Chief Justice of South Africa (2005-2016) and former anti-apartheid activist imprisoned on Robben Island.
Justice of the Constitutional Court of South Africa (2006-2017) and Acting Deputy Chief Justice.
Deputy Chief Justice of South Africa (assumed 2025) and former Judge President of the Gauteng Division.
First woman Chief Justice of South Africa (assumed 2024) and former President of the Supreme Court of Appeal.
Chief Justice of South Africa (2009-2011) and member of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission amnesty committee.
Justice of the Constitutional Court of South Africa (1994-2008) and human rights lawyer from the Transkei.
Justice of the Constitutional Court and chair of the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.
4th President of South Africa (2009-2018), leader of the ANC RET faction, and subject of numerous corruption trials.
Former Judge President of the Western Cape High Court, impeached for gross misconduct.
First President of democratic South Africa and anti-apartheid icon.
Second President of democratic South Africa (1999-2008).
5th President of South Africa and former ANC negotiator.
First President of the Constitutional Court and later Chief Justice of South Africa.
First post-apartheid Chief Justice and leading South African jurist.
First National Director of Public Prosecutions who initiated investigations into Jacob Zuma.
Financial advisor to Jacob Zuma, convicted of corruption in the Arms Deal.
Former Public Protector of South Africa who authored the 'Secure in Comfort' and 'State of Capture' reports.
Chief Justice of South Africa and chair of the Commission of Inquiry into State Capture.
Tender tycoon and director of Cat VIP Protection Services, central figure in the Madlanga Commission inquiry.
Apex court in the South African judicial system.
Second-highest court of appeal in South Africa, located in Bloemfontein.
The authority responsible for the prosecution of crime in South Africa.
Ruling political party of South Africa.
National police force of South Africa.
Commission of inquiry into allegations of state capture, fraud, and corruption in the public sector.
Judicial Commission of Inquiry into Criminality, Political Interference, and Corruption in the Criminal Justice System, established in 2025.

edges.description: Langa served as Chief Justice and Deputy President of the Constitutional Court.
Moseneke served as Deputy Chief Justice and Justice of the Constitutional Court.
Ngcobo served as Chief Justice and Justice of the Constitutional Court.
Chaskalson was the first President of the Constitutional Court and later Chief Justice.
Maya assumed the position of Chief Justice in 2024.
Zondo served as Chief Justice and Deputy Chief Justice.
Madlanga chairs the 2025 commission of inquiry into the justice system.
Madlanga served as a Justice of the Constitutional Court.
Zuma was President and Deputy President of the ANC.
The Zondo Commission investigated allegations of state capture involving Zuma.
The NPA has prosecuted Zuma on multiple fraud and corruption charges.
Langa led the Constitutional Court in lodging a complaint against Hlophe.
Hlophe attacked Moseneke during the Judicial Service Commission proceedings.
Hlophe allegedly tried to improperly influence Nkabinde in the Zuma case.
Madonsela's investigations into Nkandla and State Capture directly challenged Zuma's administration.
Shaik was Zuma's financial advisor whose conviction led to Zuma's initial dismissal.
Ngcuka initiated the first corruption investigation into Zuma.
Matlala is a central figure in the Madlanga Commission inquiry into SAPS capture.
Matlala is implicated in tender fraud and 'police capture' within the SAPS.
President Ramaphosa established and commissioned the Madlanga Commission in 2025.
Ramaphosa is the current President of the ANC.
Mbeki appointed Langa as Chief Justice.
Mandela appointed Chaskalson to lead the newly established Constitutional Court.
